name: vulkan-pra-resources
title: Vulkan stage A: resources (vendored VMA, staging uploads, VulkanMesh/VulkanTexture, samplers, blit mipmaps, deferred deletion, UpdateMesh) (issue #43, stage A)
issue:
Approved by the user 2026-10-14 with ALL recommended choices (proposal with the user's decisions: C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/vulkan-backend.md; read it FULLY first: section 1 inventory, section 2 contract (especially the 'Meshes' and 'Textures' bullets: 64-byte Vertex, uint32 indices, UpdateMesh keeps the IMesh* and is called every frame by text/particles/GpuCache, 2 frames in flight so a buffer the GPU may still read must never be overwritten, 1-4 channels, RGB8 expanded to RGBA8, sRGB, blit mipmaps only with linear-blit support), section 4 verification, the stage table in section 5 (row 'A Resources'), section 6 third-party deps (VMA: MIT, vendored under external/ at a pinned release), section 7 risks, and 'Decisions (user, 2026-10-14)': vendor VMA, built-in shaders only, N2ENGINE_RENDERER_VULKAN option, always render offscreen, CI on Linux lavapipe only with validation on and failing tests on errors/leaks, OpenGL stays the default, the editor host keeps refusing --renderer vulkan). This item is stage A 'Resources' ONLY.

PRECONDITION: start from current master AFTER PR #136 (vulkan-pr0-core, branch feat-vulkan-core-harness, stage 0) has MERGED, and re-read the then-current code before writing anything (review fixes may have renamed things; master wins over this brief). As of that branch's head (ca0161a) stage 0 introduced, and this item builds on: renderer/include/renderer/vulkan/VulkanRenderer.hpp and renderer/src/vulkan/VulkanRenderer.cpp (rewritten: ValidationMode Default/Enabled/Disabled + SetValidationMode; InitStatus NotInitialized/Ok/NoVulkanRuntime/NoSuitableDevice/ValidationUnavailable/Failed + GetInitStatus/GetInitMessage; ValidationStats {errors, warnings, otherWarnings} + GetValidationStats/GetValidationMessages/ResetValidationStats; SubmitDebugMessageForTest; GetDeviceName/GetDeviceType/GetRenderWidth/GetRenderHeight; private helpers CreateImage/DestroyImage, AllocateMemory, CreateReadbackBuffer, SubmitOneTime(recorder), LogUnsupportedOnce; MAX_FRAMES_IN_FLIGHT = 2 FrameResources {commandBuffer, fence} waited in BeginFrame; one std::mutex _mutex guarding every public method; instance apiVersion VK_API_VERSION_1_1 and devices required to be >= 1.1; colour target R8G8B8A8_UNORM resting in TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL; the IRenderer lifetime token expired by EndLifetime() in Shutdown; the header comment in the .cpp lists object lifetimes in creation order and Shutdown destroys in reverse), renderer/include/renderer/common/RendererConfig.hpp (N2ENGINE_RENDERER_VULKAN 1/0, defined PUBLIC by the renderer target), the root CMake option N2ENGINE_RENDERER_VULKAN (default ON) with renderer/CMakeLists.txt filtering /src/vulkan/ out when OFF and tests/renderer/CMakeLists.txt filtering /vulkan/ test sources out, and tests/renderer/vulkan/VulkanRendererTests.cpp with the VulkanTest fixture (NewRenderer() makes a renderer with ValidationMode::Enabled, HandleInitFailure skips on a machine without Vulkan and FAILS under N2_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1, SetUp asserts a CPU device under N2_VULKAN_EXPECT_CPU_DEVICE=1, TearDown fails the test on any validation error or validation warning of every renderer it made, which includes leaked objects at device destroy), and the CI wiring in .github/workflows/tests.yml: the Linux Clang legs (x86_64 = the required check, and arm64) install mesa-vulkan-drivers vulkan-validationlayers glslang-tools, a step pins the lavapipe ICD by glob into VK_DRIVER_FILES, and the Test step sets N2_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1 and N2_VULKAN_EXPECT_CPU_DEVICE=1; the 'linux (Release, x86_64, GCC 14)' leg configures -DN2ENGINE_RENDERER_VULKAN=OFF (no Vulkan headers installed: nothing you add may need Vulkan there); the Windows legs only compile the Vulkan code and the tests skip. The CreateMesh/CreateTexture/UpdateMesh/DestroyMesh/DestroyTexture paths are the stubs this item replaces; the test EverythingThatWouldDrawFailsCleanly must be updated so it still proves materials/shaders/draws fail cleanly while meshes and textures now work.

SCOPE: (1) Allocator: vendor AMD VulkanMemoryAllocator (MIT) at a pinned RELEASE tag (pick the latest stable v3.x release that supports Vulkan 1.1 headers as shipped by the Windows SDK action and Ubuntu 24.04 libvulkan-dev; record the exact tag and commit) as the single header vk_mem_alloc.h plus its LICENSE.txt under external/VulkanMemoryAllocator/, unmodified, and add a row to the 'Vendored (in this repository)' table of THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (name, tag/commit, path, MIT). Put VMA_IMPLEMENTATION in exactly ONE translation unit under renderer/src/vulkan/ (so it is compiled out with N2ENGINE_RENDERER_VULKAN=OFF), add the include directory to the renderer target only inside the existing if(N2ENGINE_RENDERER_VULKAN) blocks, never include vk_mem_alloc.h from a public header (keep VmaAllocator/VmaAllocation behind the .cpp or a private header so engine code and the OFF build never see it), silence VMA's own warnings locally (SYSTEM include or push/pop pragmas) without changing global flags, configure VmaAllocatorCreateInfo.vulkanApiVersion to the instance's 1.1 and choose static vs dynamic function import explicitly (document which). Create the allocator after the device and destroy it before the device in ShutdownLocked; every allocation must be freed first. Moving the stage-0 targets/readback buffer onto VMA is optional: do it only if it is low-risk, otherwise leave them on AllocateMemory and say which. (2) Staging uploads: host-visible staging buffer, copy into device-local buffers/images with correct pipeline barriers; synchronous upload through SubmitOneTime is acceptable for stage A (document the cost; a staging ring is a later optimisation), but it must be correct whether called inside or outside an open frame (BeginFrame..EndFrame). (3) VulkanMesh (implements Common::IMesh): device-local vertex buffer of Common::Vertex (64 bytes, RenderTypes.hpp) and uint32 index buffer, counts kept for stage B's IndexRange checks. CreateMesh rules mirror the software renderer and the IRenderer docs (read SoftwareRenderer.cpp and Renderer.hpp): nullptr for no vertices; meshes are tracked in a registry owned by the renderer so a FOREIGN pointer (from another renderer instance, another backend, or a test fake) is rejected: DestroyMesh is a no-op and UpdateMesh returns false. (4) UpdateMesh: keeps the same IMesh*, allocates NEW buffers on every update and retires the old ones to the deferred-deletion queue of the current frame slot (never writes a buffer the GPU may still read); returns false and changes nothing for a null mesh, a foreign mesh, or data with no vertices (docs/application.html UpdateMesh bullet). (5) VulkanTexture (implements Common::ITexture), both CreateTexture overloads, TextureOptions (renderer/include/renderer/common/TextureOptions.hpp: filter Linear/Nearest, wrap Repeat/ClampToEdge, mipmaps, srgb): channels 1 -> R8, 2 -> R8G8, 3 -> expanded to RGBA8 with alpha 255 at upload, 4 -> RGBA8; srgb selects the _SRGB variant where the device supports it for sampling (query vkGetPhysicalDeviceFormatProperties; R8/R8G8 sRGB are optional formats: fall back deterministically and document it); the image view swizzle makes a 1-channel texture sample (r,0,0,1) and a 2-channel one (r,g,0,1) exactly as OpenGL and the software renderer do (docs/application.html:316); nullptr for null data, zero width/height, channels outside 1-4, or a size over the device's maxImageDimension2D; rows are tightly packed (any width, incl. 3-channel widths not a multiple of 4). Sampler per TextureOptions (nearest/linear min/mag, mipmap mode, repeat/clamp-to-edge; anisotropy stays OFF because stage 0 does not enable samplerAnisotropy); samplers may be cached by option tuple. Mipmaps: full chain via vkCmdBlitImage ONLY when the format reports SAMPLED_IMAGE_FILTER_LINEAR + BLIT_SRC + BLIT_DST for optimal tiling, else a single level (log once); every level ends in SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL. (6) Deferred deletion: one queue per frame-in-flight slot, flushed right after BeginFrame waits that slot's fence; DestroyMesh/DestroyTexture/UpdateMesh push onto it; Shutdown waits for the device to go idle and frees all queued and all still-live meshes/textures (resources the caller never destroyed) before the allocator and device, so validation reports no leak; Destroy* or UpdateMesh on a renderer that was shut down (lifetime token expired) is a safe no-op/false. Keep the single-mutex threading model of stage 0.

TESTS (renderer_tests; new file tests/renderer/vulkan/VulkanResourceTests.cpp; if you share the VulkanTest fixture, move it into a header such as tests/renderer/vulkan/VulkanTestFixture.hpp WITHOUT changing its behaviour; every test runs with validation ON and the fixture's zero-errors/zero-warnings/no-leak teardown): mirror tests/renderer/software/SoftwareRendererResourceTests.cpp (TextureOptionsTest, UpdateMeshTest): null data, zero width/height, channels 0 and 5 return nullptr; each channel count 1-4 with srgb off/on, nearest/linear, repeat/clamp, mipmaps on/off, odd and non-power-of-two sizes (1x1, 7x5, 3-channel width 5); CreateMesh with no vertices returns nullptr; UpdateMesh keeps the pointer, rejects null/foreign/empty without changing anything; foreign pointers (a mesh/texture from a second VulkanRenderer, a fake IMesh) are ignored by Destroy*/UpdateMesh; DestroyMesh(nullptr)/DestroyTexture(nullptr) are safe; UpdateMesh every frame across many more frames than the 2 in flight, and Destroy* in the middle of an open frame (deferred deletion; validation would flag use-after-free); many (e.g. 1000) updates and create/destroy cycles return the live allocation count to its baseline (add a small test/diagnostic accessor, e.g. a VMA statistics count, documented as such); resources never destroyed before Shutdown are freed with no validation error; Destroy*/UpdateMesh after Shutdown are harmless; re-initialise after Shutdown and create again. Because nothing draws until stage B, add a test-only readback of a texture's contents (e.g. ReadTextureForTest(texture, mipLevel) copying the image into a host buffer, documented as a test hook like SubmitDebugMessageForTest) to PROVE the RGB->RGBA expansion (alpha 255), 1/2-channel data placement, exact bytes of level 0, and that blit mip levels exist with the expected sizes and plausible averaged values when mipmaps are on (and only 1 level when off or unsupported). All of these EXECUTE on lavapipe in the Linux Clang legs (N2_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1 makes a skip a failure), skip on Windows without a device, and are not built on the GCC leg (Vulkan OFF). Existing stage-0 tests must keep passing unchanged except EverythingThatWouldDrawFailsCleanly as noted.

DOCS: docs/application.html: the '#vulkan-renderer' status section becomes stage A (resources work: what exists, formats, sRGB fallback, mipmap rule, deferred deletion and why, UpdateMesh allocates new buffers per update, VMA), and update the per-method bullets that today say Vulkan creates nothing / returns false (CreateTexture with options, UpdateMesh, CreateMesh) while DrawMesh/materials/shaders still say 'draws nothing until stage B/C'; docs/testing.html: a row for the new test file and any test hooks, and the VMA dependency where third-party code is described; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md row. Keep the edits small and consistent with PR #136's wording.

DO NOT (later stages): shaders, GLSL ports, SPIR-V/glslang build step, pipelines, descriptor sets for drawing, DrawMesh/DrawObjects (stage B); materials, std140 blocks, lighting (stage C); blending/queues (D); text (E); surface/swapchain/present, GPU selection API (F); no IRenderer interface change; no change to the editor host's refusal of --renderer vulkan; OpenGL stays the default; no CI workflow change is expected (lavapipe, validation layers and the env vars already exist): if one turns out to be unavoidable, stop and report it rather than editing outside allowedPaths.

RULES: nothing builds locally on this machine; CI is the build: push and read the GitHub Actions 'Tests' workflow (8 checks; the required one is `linux (Release, x86_64, Clang)`; Windows legs compile the Vulkan code; the GCC 14 leg compiles it OUT). If something in the proposal or this brief turns out wrong (a VMA version incompatible with the headers on a leg, a format lavapipe lacks, a validation message VMA triggers), adapt minimally, list it in `deviations`, and say so; do not guess silently. UNVERIFIED (report in `unverified`): real GPU drivers (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel format support for RGB8 and sRGB blits, memory types/heaps/ReBAR), performance of one synchronous upload and one new allocation per UpdateMesh with text and particle meshes every frame, anything windowed (stage F).
acceptance: All Tests-workflow jobs green; the new Vulkan resource tests EXECUTE on lavapipe in the Linux Clang legs with validation on (zero errors/warnings, no leaks), skip on Windows without a device, and are compiled out on the GCC 14 (Vulkan OFF) leg
VMA vendored unmodified at a pinned release under external/VulkanMemoryAllocator/ with a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md row; not visible from public headers or the OFF build

CreateMesh/UpdateMesh/DestroyMesh and both CreateTexture overloads work: staging uploads, RGB->RGBA, sRGB with documented fallback, samplers per TextureOptions, blit mipmaps only with linear-blit support, null/zero/foreign inputs rejected as on the software renderer, UpdateMesh keeps the pointer and allocates new buffers, deferred deletion per frame slot
Draws, materials and shaders still fail cleanly (stage B/C); IRenderer unchanged; docs updated
notes: Reviewer: check VMA lifetime (allocator after device, destroyed before it, everything freed first), that VMA headers stay private and compile out with N2ENGINE_RENDERER_VULKAN=OFF, staging barriers and image layout transitions per mip level, the linear-blit format check, the 1/2-channel swizzles and RGB expansion, that UpdateMesh never writes a buffer a frame in flight may read and the deletion queue is flushed only after the slot's fence, foreign-pointer rejection, Shutdown frees still-live resources (validation leak check), the tests really execute on lavapipe and prove bytes via the texture readback hook, and that the stage-0 tests were not weakened.
